listing.name: Street Rod / SDL3 Port
listing.summary: Play the original DOS Street Rod with the SDL3 port and your own game data.

steps.title: Prepare a writable copy of your original game
steps.instruction: Use your own DOS Street Rod data, or get the free DOS files from the copyright owner through the link in the upstream guide. Keep SR.EXE, LIB1, LIB2 and HOT_DATA together in a writable Game copy. For optional Street Rod SE cars, keep SRSE.EXE and its matching data in Game/datadisk.

steps.title: Use the upstream Windows setup
steps.instruction: Extract the complete Windows x64 ZIP into its own folder and keep both executables and every DLL together. Open Street Rod.exe to choose your data and options. Choose original cars or Street Rod SE cars deliberately. The launcher uses the matching dataset for each.

steps.title: Register the actual player in Portcove
steps.instruction: Choose srport.exe as the existing installation and its containing directory as the working directory. Add --game-dir and your writable game-data folder as two separate arguments. For Street Rod SE, choose the datadisk folder. Review the selected player, folder and arguments, then choose Play. The separate upstream launcher can stay open or close while its game continues.

warnings: Use your own original game files. The native port includes reconstructed original program behavior and its own separately licensed port code.

references.title: Keep your settings and progress before replacing files
references.instruction: Back up HOTROD1.SAV through HOTROD15.SAV and hall_dat with each working dataset. Keep the original-car and datadisk-car folders separate so each retains its own progress. Copy %APPDATA%/Street Rod/settings.ini as well. Close both the player and launcher before replacing files. Portcove keeps a launch registration. You and upstream own runtime replacement and backups. Removing the registration leaves the working files and profile in place.

references.title: Other platforms
references.instruction: This release publishes a Windows x64 package. The publisher has no reviewed Linux, Intel Mac, Apple Silicon or Android package for this route.
